Per-frame WSG driver (interrupt handler): copies the 16-byte RAM sound-register block at #4e8c into the Namco WSG hardware registers at #5050. #4e8c is the shell/sound-engine mirror; #5050-#505f are the three voices' frequency (20-bit) and volume. Pins the RAM->hardware sound seam.

source.verbatim: 009d  218c4e    ld      hl,#4e8c	; Write freq/volume for sound regs

meaning: Voice 1 waveform-select hardware register. The driver writes the voice-1 waveform index (0-7, from RAM #4e9f/#4ecf override) to #5045; the WSG then plays WSG_WAVEFORM_<n> for voice 1.
Voice 2 waveform-select hardware register (#504a). Same role as voice 1, sourced from RAM #4eaf/#4edf.
Voice 3 waveform-select hardware register (#504f). Same role, sourced from RAM #4ebf/#4eef.

Sound engine, note-stream branch: loads the voice-1 note-stream voice-definition table pointer #3bc8 before calling the note-stream handler #2d44. The operand bytes c8 3b are the little-endian table address. Note-stream effects (tunes/melodies) live at #3bc8/#3bcc/#3bd0.
Sound engine, note-stream branch: voice-2 note-stream voice-definition table pointer #3bcc, handler #2d44.
Sound engine, note-stream branch: voice-3 note-stream voice-definition table pointer #3bd0, handler #2d44.

Sound engine, tone branch: loads the voice-1 tone voice-definition table pointer #3b30 before calling the tone handler #2dee. Operand 30 3b = LE address. One-shot SFX (munch, ghost-eaten, fruit, etc.) tone definitions live at #3b30/#3b40/#3b80.
Sound engine, tone branch: voice-2 tone voice-definition table pointer #3b40, handler #2dee.
Sound engine, tone branch: voice-3 tone voice-definition table pointer #3b80, handler #2dee.

Note-stream sound handler entry #2d44: walks a note pointer (voice def bytes 6/7), reads note bytes, treats a byte >= #f0 as a command escape (and #f<n> as a table-driven op). This is the sequencer Task 4 (start theme) decodes.

Sound engine frequency/parameter lookup table pointer #3bb0 (indexed by rst #10 from a 3-bit field of the effect byte). One of the two lookup tables that turn an effect parameter into a WSG value; Task 3/4 decode its contents.
Sound engine second lookup table pointer #3bb8 (indexed by a 4-bit field via rst #10). The companion to #3bb0; Task 3/4 decode its contents.

Tone sound handler entry #2dee: renders a tone voice definition (waveform-select via the 3-bit field -> #3bb0, frequency/duration via #3bb8) into the voice registers. This is the one-shot SFX renderer Task 3 decodes per effect.

"Choose sound N" — a sound effect is requested by writing an effect number into the RAM sound block (here #4e9c, "Choose sound 2"). The test-mode sound roster at #31a2+ exercises the effects this way; gameplay writes the same request bytes (#4eac/#4ebc). This is how the events->voice driver (Task 3) will trigger a cue.

Tone dispatch: the request byte at (ix+0)=#4e9c/#4eac/#4ebc is a BITMASK. Handler pacman.asm:2e1b-2e28 scans it high-bit-first (e=#80, b=8); the found bit's position selects the voice-def: `dec b` then `rlca` x3 makes offset = bitpos*8 into the voice's table (#3b30/#3b40/#3b80). So bit N -> the Nth 8-byte entry. Cites the `dec b` @2e32.

Background-siren stage selector entry @0e77: `ld hl,#4eac` sets up voice2's request byte, then (pacman.asm:0e7a `ld b,#e0`) masks to preserve bits5-7 while the routine sets exactly one of voice2 bits0-4 from the dots-eaten counter #4e0e by threshold (>=#e4->bit4 .. >=#74->bit1, else bit0). This chooses the 5 rising siren stages @3b40-3b60 as the maze empties. Dossier ch.3.
